what: Itaú Unibanco is the largest private bank in Latin America. It serves Brazilian households and companies with accounts, cards, loans and investments, and runs investment banking and asset management across the region.
customers: Brazilian retail customers, small businesses, corporations, and clients in Chile, Argentina, Colombia and Uruguay.
money: deposits, credit cards, personal and payroll loans
corporate lending, investment banking and treasury
insurance, pensions and asset management fees
moat: Scale in a concentrated banking market, where a handful of banks hold most Brazilian deposits, plus brand trust built over a century.
risks: Brazilian interest rates swing widely and move both margins and loan losses
Digital banks have taken market share in payments and cards
The Brazilian currency affects dollar-based returns
Political cycles affect state-owned competitors' pricing
opportunities: Return on equity above 20% is among the highest of any large bank in the world
High Brazilian rates lift income earned on its deposits
Analysts see meaningful upside to the current price
watch: Return on equity and the non-performing loan ratio.
